feat(ios): recipe filter, Switch valve countdown, widgets, Git backup, Ask Claude

From Feature-requests:
- Recipes by gear type: filter chips on the Recipes tab and the recipe
  picker, which starts with the selected brewer's type
- Hario Switch: 3-2-1 ticks with haptics before every valve change
- Home and Lock Screen widgets (beans & last brew, quick start) via an App
  Group; ldid adds the entitlement to the unsigned IPA, SideStore rewrites
  ALTAppGroups; brewlog:// links
- Git backup to GitHub, GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo: download + merge, commit
  when changed, optional auto sync; token in the Keychain
- Ask Claude for a bean with the user's own API key: brewing advice from
  the bean, gear and brews, web search for community posts with sources

Docs: parity guide, data formats, SideStore, README, Feature-requests status.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ios): extraction, water recipes, voice prompts, bean photos, label scan, grind converter

- TDS and drink weight on a brew with extraction yield, verdict and a brewing
  control chart; standalone extraction calculator (Gear -> Tools)
- Water recipes calculator (SCA, Rao, Barista Hustle, Hendon, WoC Budapest,
  Melbourne; dry minerals or 1000 ppm concentrates), water profiles saved as
  gear with GH/KH and chosen per brew
- Spoken step prompts with AVSpeechSynthesizer (Settings -> Voice), optional
  "Next, ..." announcement 5 s ahead
- Bean photos (camera or library, downsampled JPEG, roast-tinted placeholder)
  and on-device label scan with Vision that fills the bean editor
- Grind converter between calibrated grinders (filter starting point +
  micrometres per step) and the recipe's grind size shown on the selected grinder
- Backup: photos, tds, beverageWeight, waterId/waterName, waterHardness,
  waterAlkalinity, grinder.micronsPerStep; Beanconqueror tds imported
- Docs: data formats, parity matrix, feature request status, README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ios): BrewLog backup export/import and grind remembered per grinder

- Settings → Backup & import: export everything as one JSON file in the format
  shared with web and Android ({app, format, exportedAt, data, samples, machine},
  dates in ms, lowercase ids). Import merges by id and never replaces anything;
  it detects the wrapped format and the bare app data of Android exports.
  Non-UUID ids from the web app map to stable UUIDs. Everything is parsed
  leniently, sanitized and clamped (BrewLogBackup.swift).
- Switching grinders restores that grinder's own setting (set by hand after the
  last brew, else the history recommendation, else a starting value from the
  preset's defaultGrind or the typical range), like Android. No filter starting
  value for espresso.
- Tests for the format (Linux-runnable), SwiftData import/export round trip and
  grind memory.
- docs: backup format in data-formats.md, parity guide with real file paths and
  an honest feature matrix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: BOOKOO Espresso Monitor on iOS, protocol fixed on Android

The pressure sensor now follows BOOKOO's published protocol
(espresso_monitor/protocols.md, as used by Beanconqueror) on both platforms:
start 02 0C 01 00 00 00 0F, stop 02 0C 00 00 00 00 0E, 10-byte data
packets 02 1B 00 00 <bar*100 hi> <lo> <battery>. The previous Android
parser expected 20-byte 03 0B packets and dropped every real reading, and
never sent the start command after connecting.

- iOS: PressureMonitor (CoreBluetooth, demo sensor), settings sheet, pressure
  recorded with each shot (group-head sensor wins over the machine reading),
  shot timer starts when the pressure rises.
- Scale scans on both platforms ignore the monitor ("BOOKOO_EM").

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(android): read espresso recipes from the shared recipe list

The online recipe list now contains espresso recipes (method espresso, step
kinds preinfuse/extract). Without these enum values the Android feed sync
failed as a whole.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

privacy.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription: BrewLog connects to your Bluetooth coffee scale to read the weight live while you brew.
privacy.NSCameraUsageDescription: BrewLog uses the camera to photograph your coffee bag and read the details from its label. The photo stays on this device.
privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: BrewLog connects to your espresso machine (GaggiMate) in your Wi-Fi to record pressure and temperature and to start shots.
